dive. Each office is scored on four independent signals over FY2017-2026 (the
Duterte and Marcos administrations):

- **Size** — it is among the ten largest recipients of realignments;
- **Intensity** — realignments make up at least 60% of the office's enacted budget;
- **Persistence** — it received a realignment in at least eight of the ten years;
- **Tilt** — the office's realignment totals under the two administrations differ by at least ₱4B.

Every signal builds on the same yearly *realignment* — the gap between an office's
enacted and proposed budget, **GAA − NEP** (in ₱B). The tilt signal sums those yearly
realignments within each administration and takes the difference between the two totals:

**admin tilt = (total GAA − NEP across FY2017-2022) − (total GAA − NEP across FY2023-2026),**

i.e. the office's total Duterte-era realignment minus its total Marcos-era realignment. A
positive tilt means the office gained more under Duterte and is shown **red** in the chart
below; a negative tilt means it gained more under Marcos and is shown **blue**; values near
zero are grey.

Offices that trip several signals at once are the natural candidates for scrutiny.

```{r deo-screen-data}
screen_base <- deo %>%
  group_by(Office) %>%
  summarize(NEP_B         = sum(NEP_B),
            GAA_B         = sum(GAA_B),
            Insertion     = sum(Realign),
            InsShare      = sum(Realign) / sum(GAA_B),
            YearsInserted = sum(Realign > 0.5),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(
    deo %>%
      group_by(Office, Admin) %>% summarize(r = sum(Realign), .groups = "drop") %>%
      pivot_wider(names_from = Admin, values_from = r, values_fill = 0) %>%
      transmute(Office, Duterte, Marcos, Tilt = Duterte - Marcos),
    by = "Office"
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(c(Duterte, Marcos, Tilt), ~replace_na(.x, 0)))

# Newly-created district engineering offices: nothing proposed across the window (NEP = 0),
# so the realignment share is 100% by construction. Set aside and note in prose.
screen_nonep <- screen_base %>% filter(NEP_B == 0) %>% arrange(desc(GAA_B))

deo_screen <- screen_base %>%
  filter(NEP_B > 0) %>%
  mutate(
    flag_big        = min_rank(desc(Insertion)) <= 10,
    flag_intense    = InsShare >= 0.60,
    flag_persistent = YearsInserted >= n_years_deo - 2,
    flag_tilted     = abs(Tilt) >= 4,
    nflags = flag_big + flag_intense + flag_persistent + flag_tilted,
    Signals = str_c(
      if_else(flag_big,                    "large; ", ""),
      if_else(flag_intense,                "realignment-heavy; ", ""),
      if_else(flag_persistent,             "every year; ", ""),
      if_else(flag_tilted & Tilt > 0,      "Duterte-leaning; ", ""),
      if_else(flag_tilted & Tilt < 0,      "Marcos-leaning; ", "")
    ),
    Signals = str_remove(Signals, "; $")
  )

# District engineering offices whose realignment share falls below the plotted window (net trims)
screen_offscale <- deo_screen %>%
  filter(InsShare < 0) %>%
  arrange(InsShare)

offscale_note <- if (nrow(screen_offscale) == 0) {
  "none do"
} else {
  str_c(screen_offscale$Office, " (", round(screen_offscale$InsShare * 100), "%)",
        collapse = "; ")
}

nonep_note <- if (nrow(screen_nonep) == 0) {
  "none"
} else {
  str_c(screen_nonep$Office, collapse = "; ")
}
```

```{r plot-deo-screen, fig.height=5}
ggplot(deo_screen, aes(x = Insertion, y = InsShare)) +
  geom_point(aes(size = YearsInserted, fill = Tilt), shape = 21, color = "black", alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_text_repel(data = deo_screen %>% filter(nflags >= 2 | Insertion >= 9),
                  aes(label = Office), size = 2.3, max.overlaps = 30, segment.alpha = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#3994fc", mid = "grey88", high = "#ff5d6c", midpoint = 0,
                       labels = scales::comma,
                       name = "Admin tilt, PHP B\n(red = Duterte,\nblue = Marcos)") +
  scale_size(range = c(1, 6), name = "Years with a\nrealignment") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(x = "Total realignment, FY2017-2026 (PHP billions)",
       y = "Realignments as a share of the office's enacted budget",
       title = "Screening District Engineering Offices: Size and Intensity of Realignments",
       subtitle = "Top-right = both large and realignment-heavy; colour shows which administration leaned in",
       caption = "**Data Sources:** NEP and GAA documents, 2017-2026.<br>**Visualization:** AJ Montesa / People's Budget Coalition.") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9),
        plot.caption = element_markdown(size = 6),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 7), legend.text = element_text(size = 7))
```

The vertical axis starts at 0% and extends only as far as the data require. Two sets of offices fall outside it. First, `r nrow(screen_nonep)` newly-created district engineering offices had **no proposed budget** (NEP = 0) anywhere in the FY2017-2026 window, so their realignment share is 100% by construction — money Congress provided where the executive proposed nothing — and they are excluded from the scatter: `r nonep_note`. Second, `r nrow(screen_offscale)` very small offices fall *below* 0%, where the cumulative *enacted* budget came in under the proposal (a net trim rather than the padding that dominates the chart): `r offscale_note`. Because these offices are tiny, a modest peso cut reads as a large negative share, so those values are denominator artefacts more than meaningful signals.

The screen returns a consistent shortlist — none of it about a single region.
**Batangas 4th D.E. Office** is the largest single recipient of realignments —
**₱24.3B**, or **69%** of its enacted budget, padded in **all ten years** and
favoured fairly evenly by both administrations (₱14.5B Duterte, ₱9.7B Marcos), a
standing fixture regardless of who holds power. **Sorsogon** is similarly
relentless (₱16.0B, 66%, every year) but tilts Marcos-ward. **Bulacan 1st**
(₱20.7B) is the second-largest recipient and leans Marcos (₱12.7B vs ₱7.9B). At
the politically lopsided extremes sit **Abra** — the clearest Duterte-era office
(₱13.2B vs ₱3.1B) — and **Metro Manila 3rd**, its Marcos-era mirror (₱10.7B vs
₱3.8B). These offices, not any one province, are where the strongest patterns lie
and where project-level records would be worth pulling.

```{r table-deo-screen}
deo_screen %>%
  arrange(desc(nflags), desc(Insertion)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 15) %>%
  transmute(
    Office,
    `Realignment (B)`   = comma(Insertion, accuracy = 0.1),
    `Realignment share` = percent(InsShare, accuracy = 1),
    `Years realigned` = str_c(YearsInserted, "/", n_years_deo),
    `Duterte (B)`     = comma(Duterte, accuracy = 0.1),
    `Marcos (B)`      = comma(Marcos, accuracy = 0.1),
    Flags             = nflags,
    Signals
  ) %>%
  kbl(align = "lrrcrrcl",
      caption = "District engineering offices flagged for a closer look, sorted by number of signals then size") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE, font_size = 12) %>%
  column_spec(8, width = "13em")
```

# The FY 2027 Proposal

The FY 2027 National Expenditure Program is the live budget document now before
Congress — the one advocates can still shape. The proposal's figures already run
through the tables and charts in the sections above; this section draws them
together in one place: the proposal's overall size, its distribution **by program**
and **by district engineering office**, and how it compares to the two most useful
benchmarks — what the Executive proposed for FY 2026 (the previous **NEP**) and
what Congress actually enacted (the previous **GAA**).

## FY 2027 in Context: Comparison with FY 2026

At **₱642.6B**, the FY 2027 proposal sits between the two FY 2026 figures. It is
about **₱113B _above_** the ₱529.6B that was finally enacted for 2026 — a budget
slashed by the roughly ₱350B flood-control cut — but about **₱237B _below_** the
₱880B the Executive had originally proposed for 2026. In other words, the
Department is proposing to spend more than the shrunken 2026 law allows, but well
short of its own ambitions a year earlier.

```{r plot-2627-compare, fig.height=5.2}
cmp <- byprogram %>%
  filter(FY %in% c(2026, 2027)) %>%
  transmute(Program,
            `NEP 2026` = if_else(FY == 2026, NEP_B, NA_real_),
            `GAA 2026` = if_else(FY == 2026, GAA_B, NA_real_),
            `NEP 2027` = if_else(FY == 2027, NEP_B, NA_real_)) %>%
  group_by(Program) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_longer(-Program, names_to = "Series", values_to = "AmountB") %>%
  mutate(Series = factor(Series, levels = c("NEP 2026", "GAA 2026", "NEP 2027")),
         Program = factor(Program, levels = dpwh_programs))

ggplot(cmp, aes(x = AmountB, y = fct_rev(Program), fill = Series)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.7) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.06))) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = function(x) str_wrap(x, 24)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("NEP 2026" = "#ffd0d5", "GAA 2026" = "#3994fc", "NEP 2027" = "#c0392b")) +
  labs(x = "PHP billions", y = NULL, fill = NULL,
       title = "FY 2027 Proposal vs FY 2026, by Program",
       subtitle = "Light pink = FY2026 proposed; blue = FY2026 enacted; red = FY2027 proposed",
       caption = "**Data Sources:** NEP and GAA documents.<br>**Visualization:** AJ Montesa / People's Budget Coalition.") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "top", panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9), plot.caption = element_markdown(size = 6),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8))
```

Read program by program, the FY 2027 proposal looks far more like the FY 2026
*proposal* than the FY 2026 *enacted* budget — the Executive is, in effect,
re-proposing much of what Congress rearranged on the way to the 2026 GAA:

- **Flood Management**, gutted to just **₱4.8B** in the 2026 GAA, is restored to
  **₱103.5B** in the FY 2027 proposal (though still below its ₱250.8B FY2026 NEP).
- **Network Development**, which Congress cut to **₱96.8B** on enactment, returns
  to **₱176.6B** — close to its original FY2026 proposal.
- The **Convergence and Special Support Program** — which Congress *inflated* to
  **₱240.5B** on enactment — is proposed back down at **₱157.3B**, roughly its
  FY2026 proposed level.

The full comparison, with the proposed change measured against the enacted 2026
budget (the current baseline):

```{r table-2627-compare}
byprogram %>%
  filter(FY %in% c(2026, 2027)) %>%
  group_by(Program) %>%
  summarise(`NEP 2026` = sum(NEP_B[FY == 2026], na.rm = TRUE),
            `GAA 2026` = sum(GAA_B[FY == 2026], na.rm = TRUE),
            `NEP 2027` = sum(NEP_B[FY == 2027], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(`Chg. vs 2026 GAA` = `NEP 2027` - `GAA 2026`,
         Program = factor(Program, levels = dpwh_programs)) %>%
  arrange(desc(`NEP 2027`)) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 1))) %>%
  kbl(align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
      caption = "FY 2027 Proposed New Appropriations vs FY 2026, by Program (PHP billions)") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE, font_size = 12) %>%
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE)
```


## By Program: Proposed and Enacted Levels

Zooming in on the programs, it helps to see the **overall levels** the Executive
proposes and the legislature enacts — the raw distribution of pesos across
programs, and where the **FY 2027 proposal** places them relative to the recent
past.

At the department level, the FY 2027 NEP proposes **₱642.6B** — a marked step
down from the ₱880B proposed for 2026 and the ₱1,087.7B *enacted* for 2025 (the
2025 figure is the post-veto total; see the veto section). The proposed-versus-enacted
totals over the full window make the swings plain:

```{r plot-levels-total, fig.height=3.8}
totlevels <- byprogram %>%
  group_by(FY) %>%
  summarise(NEP = sum(NEP_B, na.rm = TRUE),
            GAA = if (all(is.na(GAA_B))) NA_real_ else sum(GAA_B, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_longer(c(NEP, GAA), names_to = "Item", values_to = "AmountB") %>%
  filter(!is.na(AmountB)) %>%
  mutate(Item = factor(Item, levels = c("NEP", "GAA")))

ggplot(totlevels, aes(x = FY, y = AmountB, colour = Item, group = Item)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) + geom_point(size = 1.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(AmountB)), vjust = -0.8, size = 2.4, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(seq(2018, 2026, 2), 2027)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.14))) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("NEP" = "#ffa6b0", "GAA" = "#3994fc")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "PHP billions", colour = NULL,
       title = "DPWH Total New Appropriations: Proposed (NEP) vs Enacted (GAA)",
       caption = "**Note:** FY2027 shows the NEP only (not yet enacted). FY2025 GAA is the post-veto total.<br>**Visualization:** AJ Montesa / People's Budget Coalition.") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
        plot.caption = element_markdown(size = 6))
```

The enacted budget ran *above* the proposal every year from 2020 to 2025 — a
legislature adding to the President's plan — until FY2026, when the enacted
total fell far *below* the proposal (the ₱246B flood-control cut). The FY2027
proposal resets the level near ₱643B.

**How is the FY 2027 proposal distributed across programs?** Two programs account
for more than half of it: Network Development (₱176.6B, 27%) and the
Convergence and Special Support Program (₱157.3B, 25%) — the latter
historically the *discretionary* program that Congress inflated through
realignments, now proposed at a high level in the Executive's own document.

```{r plot-levels-byprogram, fig.height=5.0}
lvl <- byprogram %>%
  select(FY, Program, NEP_B, GAA_B) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(NEP_B, GAA_B), names_to = "Item", values_to = "AmountB") %>%
  mutate(Item = factor(if_else(Item == "NEP_B", "NEP (proposed)", "GAA (enacted)"),
                       levels = c("NEP (proposed)", "GAA (enacted)"))) %>%
  filter(!is.na(AmountB))

ggplot(lvl, aes(x = FY, y = AmountB, fill = Program)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72) +
  facet_wrap(~Item, ncol = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(seq(2018, 2026, 2), 2027)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.04))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = program_colors) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "PHP billions", fill = NULL,
       title = "DPWH Budget Levels by Program: Proposed (NEP, to 2027) and Enacted (GAA, to 2026)",
       caption = "**Note:** FY2027 GAA is omitted (not yet enacted). Each bar is the full department budget, split by program.<br>**Visualization:** AJ Montesa / People's Budget Coalition.") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.text = element_text(size = 6.5),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
        plot.caption = element_markdown(size = 6),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold")) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
```

Reading the two panels together is instructive. In the **enacted** budgets (lower
panel), the Convergence and Special Support Program balloons after 2022 — the
realignment story documented in Section 6. But the **proposed** budgets (upper
panel) show the Executive itself steadily raising Convergence, so that by FY2027
it is proposed at ₱157B before Congress touches it. The proposed FY2027
distribution, in full:

```{r table-levels-2027}
byprogram %>%
  filter(FY == 2027) %>%
  transmute(Program,
            `NEP 2027 (PHP B)` = round(NEP_B, 1),
            `Share of proposal` = scales::percent(NEP_B / sum(NEP_B), accuracy = 0.1)) %>%
  arrange(desc(`NEP 2027 (PHP B)`)) %>%
  kbl(align = c("l", "r", "r"),
      caption = "FY 2027 Proposed New Appropriations by Program (NEP)") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE, font_size = 12)
```


## Inside the Proposal: The Biggest Line Items

Applying the same granular lens to the **FY 2027 proposal** shows what the Executive
is prioritising *within* the programs. The largest proposed items are a telling mix
of the national works Congress usually trims and the district-oriented items it
usually adds.

```{r plot-2027-items, fig.height=5.4}
items27 <- gran %>%
  filter(FY == 2027, NEP_B > 0) %>%
  group_by(Item, Program) %>% summarise(NEP_B = sum(NEP_B, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  slice_max(NEP_B, n = 15) %>%
  mutate(ProgLab = str_replace(Program, "Convergence and Special Support Program", "Convergence & Special Support") %>%
                   str_replace(" Program$",""),
         ItemS = short_item(Item), ItemS = fct_reorder(ItemS, NEP_B))
ggplot(items27, aes(x = NEP_B, y = ItemS, fill = ProgLab)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.74) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(NEP_B)), hjust = -0.15, size = 2.7, colour = "grey20") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.10))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = program_colors_short, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "FY 2027 proposed NEP (PHP billions)", y = NULL,
       title = "The 15 biggest line items in the FY 2027 proposal",
       subtitle = "Coloured by program; a mix of national road works and Convergence district items",
       caption = "**Data:** granular program encoding.<br>**Visualization:** AJ Montesa / People's Budget Coalition.") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.text = element_text(size = 6.5),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9), plot.caption = element_markdown(size = 6),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7.5)) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
```

The single largest proposed item is **By-Pass & Diversion Roads (₱127B)** — a
national Network Development line that Congress has historically *cut* by the most
(recall the ₱94B cumulative reduction above). Right behind it is **BIP – Access
Roads to Public Buildings (₱106B)**, a Convergence item of exactly the type
Congress historically *adds*. The two big flood-mitigation lines return at ₱63B and
₱41B. In other words, the FY 2027 NEP re-proposes a large national road-and-flood
program — much of which the legislature has a track record of trimming in favour
of district items — setting up the same proposal-versus-enactment tug-of-war at
the item level that the rest of this report documents at the program and district
levels.

## By District Engineering Office: The Proposed Distribution

Having seen how Congress has historically built up district budgets, it is worth
turning the same geographic lens on the **FY 2027 proposal**. Its starting
distribution across operating units is strikingly centralized — a reminder that
the district-level build-up documented above happens *after* the proposal, not in
it.

Of the ₱642.6B proposed for FY 2027, **₱510.0B (79%) sits in the Central Office**
and only **₱129.7B (20%) is distributed across the 198 district engineering
offices** (the small remainder is in regional and other units). That 79/20 split
is the raw material Congress works on: the district-level build-up that defines
DPWH's budget politics happens *later*, in the move from proposal to enacted law.

```{r plot-levels-centraldist, fig.height=3.8}
unit_levels <- byoperunit %>%
  mutate(Unit = case_when(Office == "Central Office"        ~ "Central Office",
                          str_detect(Office, "D.E. Office") ~ "District Engineering Offices",
                          str_detect(Office, "Regional")    ~ "Regional Offices",
                          TRUE                              ~ "Other units")) %>%
  filter(FY >= 2018) %>%
  group_by(FY, Unit) %>%
  summarise(NEP_B = sum(NEP_B, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(FY) %>% mutate(share = NEP_B / sum(NEP_B)) %>% ungroup() %>%
  mutate(Unit = factor(Unit, levels = c("Central Office", "District Engineering Offices",
                                         "Regional Offices", "Other units")))

ggplot(unit_levels, aes(x = FY, y = share, fill = Unit)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.74) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(seq(2018, 2026, 2), 2027)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Central Office" = "#3994fc",
                               "District Engineering Offices" = "#ffa6b0",
                               "Regional Offices" = "#bcbef2", "Other units" = "#d9d9d9")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Share of proposed NEP", fill = NULL,
       title = "Where the Proposal Places the Money: NEP Share by Operating Unit",
       caption = "**Note:** Each bar is the FY's *proposed* (NEP) new appropriations, split by operating unit. FY2027 is proposed only.<br>**Visualization:** AJ Montesa / People's Budget Coalition.") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12.5),
        plot.caption = element_markdown(size = 6)) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1))
```

At proposal stage the Central Office has held the overwhelming share of new
appropriations every year — typically 75-85% — because the Executive budgets
most district projects centrally and lets the release-and-realignment machinery
distribute them. The FY2027 proposal (79% central) is squarely in that pattern.

**Which districts fare best in the proposal?** Even within the 20% that is
pre-allocated to named districts, the FY2027 NEP is concentrated: the top office
is proposed ₱3.5B while the median district gets a fraction of that.

```{r plot-levels-topdeo, fig.height=5.0}
top_deo_27 <- deo_all %>%
  filter(FY == 2027) %>%
  slice_max(NEP_B, n = 20) %>%
  mutate(Office = str_remove(Office, " D\\.E\\. Office$") %>% str_remove(" Engineering$"),
         Office = fct_reorder(Office, NEP_B))

ggplot(top_deo_27, aes(x = NEP_B, y = Office)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#3994fc", width = 0.72) +
  geom_text(aes(label = format(round(NEP_B, 2), nsmall = 2)), hjust = -0.15, size = 2.6) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(x = "FY 2027 proposed NEP (PHP billions)", y = NULL,
       title = "Top 20 District Engineering Offices in the FY 2027 Proposal",
       caption = "**Note:** Pre-allocated district amounts in the NEP, before congressional realignment.<br>**Visualization:** AJ Montesa / People's Budget Coalition.") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12.5),
        plot.caption = element_markdown(size = 6),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7))
```

The offices proposed the most in FY2027 — Bulacan 2nd (₱3.5B), Metro Manila 3rd
(₱2.9B), Nueva Ecija 1st (₱2.8B) — are a mix of high-population and
infrastructure-heavy districts. But the more important point for scrutiny is the
gap between this proposed geography and the *enacted* one: as the realignment
analysis above shows, Congress adds heavily to district offices during
deliberations, so the enacted distribution of DPWH money will look very different
from this proposal.


# The Line-Item Vetoes: 2019 and 2025

Twice in this window the President reached past Congress's realignments and struck
enacted amounts out of the DPWH budget by **line-item veto** — in **FY2019
(₱95.4B)** and again in **FY2025 (₱26.1B)**. In both years the pattern was the
same: Congress inflated the proposal (heavily in 2019's Local Program, and in
2025's Convergence and Flood programs), and the President then vetoed a large
block of it, almost all from the **Central Office**. The enacted GAA used
throughout this report is the **post-veto** figure in both years.

## The 2019 Veto (₱95.4B)

In FY2019, Congress raised the DPWH's New Appropriations only modestly in
aggregate (from a **₱544.5B** proposal to a **₱549.4B** legislated total) but **heavily
reallocated** the money — above all into the Local Program. The President then
exercised **line-item vetoes worth ₱95.37B**, almost all of it from that program,
bringing the enacted GAA down to **₱454.0B** (the NEP-to-GAA dip visible back in
Section 1). The three stages below are what the President **proposed** (NEP), what
Congress **legislated** (the pre-veto total), and what was finally **enacted**
after the line-item veto.

```{r plot-veto-total, fig.height=3.6}
veto_total <- tibble(
  Stage = factor(c("Proposed\n(NEP)", "Legislated\n(pre-veto)", "Enacted\n(post-veto)"),
                 levels = c("Proposed\n(NEP)", "Legislated\n(pre-veto)", "Enacted\n(post-veto)")),
  AmountB = c(sum(byprogram$NEP_B[byprogram$FY == 2019]),
              sum(byprogram$GAA_B[byprogram$FY == 2019]) + sum(byprogram$Veto_B[byprogram$FY == 2019]),
              sum(byprogram$GAA_B[byprogram$FY == 2019]))
)

ggplot(veto_total, aes(x = Stage, y = AmountB, fill = Stage)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.62) +
  geom_text(aes(label = comma(AmountB, accuracy = 0.1)), vjust = -0.5, size = 3) +
  annotate("segment", x = 2, xend = 3, y = 575, yend = 575) +
  annotate("text", x = 2.5, y = 590, label = "vetoed: -P95.4B", size = 3, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#ffa6b0", "#bcbef2", "#3994fc")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "PHP billions",
       title = "DPWH FY2019: Proposed -> Legislated -> Enacted (after the Veto)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8))
```

```{r plot-veto-byprogram, fig.height=4.6}
veto_prog <- byprogram %>%
  filter(FY == 2019) %>%
  transmute(Program,
            `Proposed (NEP)`        = NEP_B,
            `Legislated (pre-veto)` = GAA_B + Veto_B,
            `Enacted (post-veto)`   = GAA_B) %>%
  pivot_longer(-Program, names_to = "Stage", values_to = "AmountB") %>%
  mutate(Stage   = factor(Stage, levels = c("Proposed (NEP)", "Legislated (pre-veto)", "Enacted (post-veto)")),
         Program = factor(Program, levels = dpwh_programs))

ggplot(veto_prog, aes(x = Stage, y = AmountB, fill = Stage)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~Program, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4, labeller = label_wrap_gen(22)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Proposed (NEP)" = "#ffa6b0", "Legislated (pre-veto)" = "#bcbef2",
                               "Enacted (post-veto)" = "#3994fc")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "PHP billions", fill = NULL,
       title = "FY2019 by Program: Proposed, Legislated, and Enacted after the Veto",
       caption = "**Data Sources:** NEP, legislated GAA, and veto message, FY2019.<br>**Visualization:** AJ Montesa / People's Budget Coalition.") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
        plot.caption = element_markdown(size = 6),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white"), strip.text = element_text(size = 6.5),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1, size = 6),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6.5))
```

The veto was overwhelmingly a **Local Program** event: only that program (plus
token amounts in the two overhead lines) shows a legislated (pre-veto) bar towering over the
enacted level. Unpacking the vetoed line items by **type of work** and by **engineering
office** shows where the realigned money had been parked:

```{r load-veto-detail}
veto_detail <- read_xlsx(data_path, sheet = "2019_Veto") %>%
  mutate(Veto_B = GAA_Veto / 1e9)
```

```{r plot-veto-activity, fig.height=3.8}
veto_detail %>%
  group_by(Activity) %>%
  summarize(Veto_B = sum(Veto_B), .groups = "drop") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Veto_B, y = fct_reorder(Activity, Veto_B))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#3994fc") +
  geom_text(aes(label = format(round(Veto_B, 1), nsmall = 1)), hjust = -0.15, size = 2.6) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(x = "PHP billions vetoed", y = NULL,
       title = "What the 2019 Veto Struck, by Type of Work",
       caption = "**Data Source:** FY2019 veto message.<br>**Visualization:** AJ Montesa / People's Budget Coalition.") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
        plot.caption = element_markdown(size = 6),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8))
```

```{r plot-veto-office, fig.height=4.4}
veto_detail %>%
  group_by(Office) %>%
  summarize(Veto_B = sum(Veto_B), .groups = "drop") %>%
  slice_max(Veto_B, n = 15) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Veto_B, y = fct_reorder(Office, Veto_B))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#ffa6b0") +
  geom_text(aes(label = format(round(Veto_B, 2), nsmall = 2)), hjust = -0.15, size = 2.4) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.14))) +
  labs(x = "PHP billions vetoed", y = NULL,
       title = "Where the 2019 Veto Struck: Top 15 Offices",
       subtitle = "The DPWH Central Office alone accounts for ~P74B of the P95.4B vetoed",
       caption = "**Data Source:** FY2019 veto message.<br>**Visualization:** AJ Montesa / People's Budget Coalition.") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9),
        plot.caption = element_markdown(size = 6),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7.5))
```

```{r table-veto-program}
byprogram %>%
  filter(FY == 2019) %>%
  transmute(Program,
            `Proposed (NEP)`        = NEP_B,
            `Legislated (pre-veto)` = GAA_B + Veto_B,
            `Vetoed`                = Veto_B,
            `Enacted (post-veto)`   = GAA_B) %>%
  bind_rows(tibble(Program = "DPWH TOTAL",
                   `Proposed (NEP)` = sum(byprogram$NEP_B[byprogram$FY == 2019]),
                   `Legislated (pre-veto)` = sum((byprogram$GAA_B + byprogram$Veto_B)[byprogram$FY == 2019]),
                   Vetoed = sum(byprogram$Veto_B[byprogram$FY == 2019]),
                   `Enacted (post-veto)` = sum(byprogram$GAA_B[byprogram$FY == 2019]))) %>%
  mutate(across(-Program, ~comma(.x, accuracy = 0.1))) %>%
  kbl(align = c("l", rep("r", 4)),
      caption = "FY2019 DPWH: proposed, legislated (pre-veto), vetoed, and enacted (post-veto) --- PHP billions") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE, font_size = 12) %>%
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE)
```

```{r table-veto-activity}
veto_detail %>%
  group_by(Activity) %>%
  summarize(`Vetoed (PHP B)` = sum(Veto_B), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(`Vetoed (PHP B)`)) %>%
  mutate(`Share of veto` = percent(`Vetoed (PHP B)` / sum(`Vetoed (PHP B)`), accuracy = 0.1),
         `Vetoed (PHP B)` = comma(`Vetoed (PHP B)`, accuracy = 0.01)) %>%
  kbl(align = "lrr",
      caption = "FY2019 vetoed line items, by type of work") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE, font_size = 12)
```

## The 2025 Veto (₱26.1B)

FY2025 repeated the pattern on a smaller scale. Congress raised the DPWH proposal
sharply — from a **₱898.9B** NEP to a **₱1,113.8B** legislated total, a **+₱215B**
insertion — and the President then vetoed **₱26.1B**, bringing the enacted GAA
to **₱1,087.7B**. Where 2019's veto fell on the Local Program, 2025's landed
squarely on the two programs most associated with discretionary spending:
**Convergence and Special Support (₱18.0B vetoed)** and **Flood Management
(₱7.5B)**.

```{r plot-veto2025-total, fig.height=3.6}
veto_total_25 <- tibble(
  Stage = factor(c("Proposed\n(NEP)", "Legislated\n(pre-veto)", "Enacted\n(post-veto)"),
                 levels = c("Proposed\n(NEP)", "Legislated\n(pre-veto)", "Enacted\n(post-veto)")),
  AmountB = c(sum(byprogram$NEP_B[byprogram$FY == 2025]),
              sum(byprogram$GAA_B[byprogram$FY == 2025]) + sum(byprogram$Veto_B[byprogram$FY == 2025]),
              sum(byprogram$GAA_B[byprogram$FY == 2025]))
)

ggplot(veto_total_25, aes(x = Stage, y = AmountB, fill = Stage)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.62) +
  geom_text(aes(label = comma(AmountB, accuracy = 0.1)), vjust = -0.5, size = 3) +
  annotate("segment", x = 2, xend = 3, y = 1150, yend = 1150) +
  annotate("text", x = 2.5, y = 1175, label = "vetoed: -P26.1B", size = 3, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#ffa6b0", "#bcbef2", "#3994fc")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "PHP billions",
       title = "DPWH FY2025: Proposed -> Legislated -> Enacted (after the Veto)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8))
```

The vetoed amounts fell on three programs, and — as in 2019 — almost entirely
on centrally-held appropriations:

```{r plot-veto2025-detail, fig.height=3.4}
veto25_prog <- byprogram %>%
  filter(FY == 2025, Veto_B > 0) %>%
  transmute(Program = factor(Program, levels = dpwh_programs), Veto_B) %>%
  arrange(desc(Veto_B))

central_share_25 <- read_xlsx(data_path, sheet = "2025_Veto") %>%
  summarise(sh = sum(GAA_Veto[Office == "Central Office"], na.rm = TRUE) /
                 sum(GAA_Veto, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% pull(sh)

ggplot(veto25_prog, aes(x = Veto_B, y = fct_reorder(Program, Veto_B))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#8c8c8c", width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = comma(Veto_B, accuracy = 0.1)), hjust = -0.15, size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = function(x) str_wrap(x, 24)) +
  labs(x = "Vetoed (PHP billions)", y = NULL,
       title = "FY2025 Line-Item Veto, by Program (₱26.1B total)",
       subtitle = sprintf("The Central Office accounts for ~₱25.1B (%.0f%%) of the amount vetoed",
                          100 * central_share_25),
       caption = "**Data Source:** FY2025 veto message.<br>**Visualization:** AJ Montesa / People's Budget Coalition.") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12.5),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9), plot.caption = element_markdown(size = 6),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8))
```

As in 2019, the veto was overwhelmingly a **Central Office** event — about
**₱25.1B (96%)** of the ₱26.1B struck was drawn from centrally-held appropriations,
with only token amounts removed from named district offices. The recurring story
is the same across both years: the largest discretionary build-ups are inserted
centrally during deliberations, and it is there that the veto pen, when used,
falls.


# DPWH and the Unprogrammed Appropriations

The **Unprogrammed Appropriations (UA)** is a standby fund that may only be
released when revenue collections exceed targets or new financing is secured.
Because releases happen *outside* the regular program structure, they are harder
to track — and the DPWH's draw on the UA has become a focus of scrutiny, as a
number of flood-control projects later flagged as questionable were reportedly
financed through this route. The table records **allotments released** (the
spending authority granted) and **obligations** (amounts actually committed);
obligation data before 2013 could not be sourced, and FY2015-2017 carried no UA
releases to the DPWH at all.

```{r load-ua}
ua <- read_xlsx(data_path, sheet = "DPWH_UA") %>%
  mutate(Allotments_B  = Allotments / 1e6,    # thousand pesos -> PHP billions
         Obligations_B = Obligations / 1e6)

ua_long <- ua %>%
  select(FY, Allotments_B, Obligations_B) %>%
  pivot_longer(-FY, names_to = "Item", values_to = "AmountB") %>%
  mutate(Item = recode(Item, Allotments_B = "Allotments", Obligations_B = "Obligations"),
         Item = factor(Item, levels = c("Allotments", "Obligations")))
```

```{r plot-ua, fig.height=4.2}
ggplot(ua_long %>% filter(!is.na(AmountB)), aes(x = FY, y = AmountB, fill = Item)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.66) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2011:2025) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.06))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Allotments" = "#ffa6b0", "Obligations" = "#3994fc")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "PHP billions", fill = NULL,
       title = "DPWH Releases from the Unprogrammed Appropriations",
       subtitle = "Allotments released and obligations incurred, by fiscal year",
       caption = "**Data Sources:** DBM allotment and obligation records, 2011-2025.<br>**Visualization:** AJ Montesa / People's Budget Coalition.") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.15, 0.75),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9),
        plot.caption = element_markdown(size = 6),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7))
```

After a decade of negligible draws, UA releases to the DPWH surged from **₱16B in
2022 to ₱89B in 2023 and ₱245B in 2024** — the latter alone roughly a quarter of
the department's entire regular budget that year. Yet a large share of these
allotments went unobligated (about **54% utilised in 2024**, **50% in 2025**),
which — alongside the project-level findings reported elsewhere — is exactly the
kind of pattern that merits questioning at the hearings.

```{r table-ua}
ua %>%
  transmute(FY,
            `Allotments (B)`  = Allotments_B,
            `Obligations (B)` = Obligations_B,
            Utilization       = Obligations_B / Allotments_B) %>%
  mutate(
    `Allotments (B)`  = comma(`Allotments (B)`, accuracy = 0.01),
    `Obligations (B)` = ifelse(is.na(`Obligations (B)`), "\u2013",
                               comma(`Obligations (B)`, accuracy = 0.01)),
    Utilization       = ifelse(is.na(Utilization) | is.nan(Utilization) | is.infinite(Utilization),
                               "\u2013", percent(Utilization, accuracy = 1))
  ) %>%
  kbl(align = "lrrr",
      caption = "DPWH releases from the Unprogrammed Appropriations, PHP billions") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE, font_size = 12)
```

# Notes

**On coverage.** The Section 1 series is intentionally left with gaps where the
physical documents have not yet been encoded; points mark observed years. The
by-operating-unit data now runs from the FY2014 budget through FY2026, so the
department-wide comparisons span the 16th through 20th Congresses and seven House
Speakers (see the Speaker table in the operating-unit section). The district-office
deep-dives center on the Duterte and Marcos administrations (FY2017 onward —
ten budgets, 2019 included), though the realignments-by-Congress chart reaches back
to the 16th Congress (the three Aquino-era budgets) for context. The FY2019 figures
use the enacted, post-veto GAA; the ₱95.4B line-item veto that year is isolated in
its own chart and section.

**On the 2019 GAA.** The GAA figures throughout are the **enacted, post-veto**
levels (they reconcile to the Office-of-the-Secretary totals in Section 1).
"Legislated (pre-veto)" reconstructs what Congress passed by adding the vetoed
amounts back to the enacted GAA. Because of this, every 2019 realignment figure in
this document reflects the *combined* effect of Congress's reallocation and the
President's veto, not Congress alone; the veto section, the Central-vs-District veto
chart, and the grey segments in the realignments-by-Congress chart isolate the veto
and recover Congress's pre-veto intent.

**On the Unprogrammed Appropriations.** UA obligation data before 2013 could not
